record: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map of Oakland, 1911–12, vol. 1, Library of Congress
facts: The Key Route Inn spanned the terminus. The survey diagrams north and south hotel ranges, a broad 1st-story opening at the Broadway approach, rooms above and a train shed between Valley Street and the hotel.

record: City of Oakland, Eastline Project EIR, Historic Resources Analysis, B-8 to B-9
facts: The 1907 Tudor Revival complex housed the Key System station, hotel, dining room and park. Its site was repurposed to extend Grand Avenue across the former rail route by 1935.

record: San Francisco Planning, Landmark Designation Case Report, 42
facts: Architects Oliver and Foulkes designed the Key Route Inn at Broadway and Grand Avenue. It is demolished.

record: Greater Oakland, 1911, edited by Evarts I. Blake, printed page 291, archived book leaf 306
facts: The photograph shows the Broadway elevation, the Tudor gables and two different clockless tower crowns.
